text:
Priya Nair: Heads-up  Dedicated pool autoscaler misapplied a safety throttle rule during last night's policy push. A small set of reserved customers are seeing sustained lower throughput on model inference (timeouts and queued requests). Two of those are next-quarter renewals.

Owen Park: How many tenants and what degree of impact?

Priya Nair: 7 tenants affected; impact ranges from 10-40% throughput degradation depending on batch size. Engineers have a hotfix to relax the safety threshold and a plan to add burst credits to the affected pools. ETA to restore baseline ~45-60 minutes with partial relief in ~20.

Marta Ruiz: We need three comms: (1) brief notice to all affected tenants, (2) tailored outreach to the 2 renewals with offer for a dedicated remediation call and prioritized capacity, (3) an internal one-pager with credit approval language for AEs. Tone should be apologetic but confident.

Ben Cho: For the renewals, recommend we proactively offer a one-time usage credit and a 1-week prioritized capacity window post-fix to run any backfills. Avoid specific dollar amounts in the public note.

Jules Martin (Legal): Confirmed. Suggested legal line: "We will evaluate eligibility for service credits consistent with your agreement; your account team will follow up to confirm any applicable credits or accommodations." Do not promise concrete credits in the first message.

Priya Nair: Draft customer-facing blurb below (short). Please comment.

```
Hi [Customer],

Were reaching out to let you know we detected reduced inference throughput affecting some Dedicated capacity pools overnight. Our engineers traced this to a safety throttle rule introduced in a recent autoscaler config update and are deploying a fix now. We expect normal throughput to return within ~45-60 minutes; partial relief is expected sooner.

What were doing:
- Rolling a targeted autoscaler fix to remove the misapplied throttle.
- Applying prioritized burst capacity for affected pools to reduce queued requests.
- Monitoring your tenant and prioritizing any urgent backfill or replay work.

Next steps: your CS lead will follow up with an account-specific update and to coordinate any remediation or credits. You can follow the incident at <status.redwood.ai/inc/INC-2026-2100>.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

Priya, Customer Success
```

Owen Park: LGTM. For the renewal cohort add: "We're available for a dedicated remediation call and will prioritize capacity for any necessary replays  please reply with preferred times this week."

Marta Ruiz: I'll assemble the AE one-pager with impacted tenants, sample graphs (rps, queue depth), suggested credit phrasing, and an approval checklist so AEs can request exec sign-off quickly.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-2100 created (priority: high). Hotfix rollout started. Postmortem scheduled tomorrow 11:30 AM PT.

Ben Cho: I'll own the 1:1 outreach to the renewal accounts and coordinate the remediation calls. Marta  please link the approval checklist in the message so I can move quickly.

Jules Martin (Legal): Approved initial wording. Keep the public note high level; reserve specifics for 1:1s.

Priya Nair: Also proposing a short feedback capture form for affected tenants to report any residual issues and whether they accepted remediation offers. Will link it in the follow-up.

Owen Park: Good call. Once hotfix is verified, CS ops please send a follow-up update to affected tenants and mark the incident resolved in status pages.

Priya Nair: Agreed  tracking actions now. Sending initial note in 10m after legal ack. :white_check_mark:
